newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac calls fifth early election since 1958.
newsitem.headline: Chirac calls fifth early election since 1958.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac's decision to stage parliamentary elections on May 25 and June 1 marks the fifth time the National Assembly has been dissolved early since the start of the Fifth Republic in 1958.

Under the constitution, the French president can call a parliamentary election whenever he wants, but opposition parties accuse Chirac of misusing a power only used to resolve deep crises in the past.
The following are the previous cases of early dissolution:

October 1962 - President Charles de Gaulle dissolves parliament after it blocks his plan to introduce presidential elections by universal suffrage. De Gaulle subsequently wins a referendum on his planned electoral reform.
May 1968 - De Gaulle calls early elections as part of a scheme to defuse student and worker uprising.
May 1981 - Socialist Francois Mitterrand wins presidential election, dissolves parliament dominated by centre-right and wins a majority to carry out a strongly left-wing agenda.
May 1988 - Mitterrand wins new term, repeats dissolution of 1981. His Socialist party makes gains but not enough to secure an absolute majority.
